title: Hepatovirus Coverage Audit
h1: Does the hepatitis A virus module work?
standfirst: Hepatovirus is the genus of hepatitis A virus, still a notifiable cause of acute liver disease worldwide and vaccine-preventable since 1995. The genus also holds bat, rodent, hedgehog, seal and bird hepatoviruses described in the last decade. This audit covers the module built for it, which was rebuilt on 5 October because it was the thinnest-trained of the ten.
headline_tiles: vocabulary collapse at equal proteins sampled

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: One genus, 37 species, and the same layout as Enterovirus.

blocks.html: The hepatovirus polyprotein is VP4, VP2, VP3, VP1, 2A, 2B, 2C, 3A, VPg, 3C and 3D. There is no leader and VP0 is cleaved, which is the organisation Enterovirus has and which separates both from the VP0-uncleaved group that holds Parechovirus, Kobuvirus and Avihepatovirus.

rows: genomes in the BV-BRC protein dump

blocks.html: The sampling is lopsided. BV-BRC holds 1,718 genomes but only 919 unique protein sequences, because hepatitis A virus is sequenced repeatedly and the non-primate hepatoviruses hardly at all. Most of the 37 species contribute one or two genomes.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Rebuilt on 5 October: the thinnest-trained module in the family, roughly doubled.

blocks.html: Before the rebuild this module had 42 profiles across twelve features, built from barely 340 annotated mature peptides. Several features had fewer than twenty training sequences: VPg had 9, 2B had 13, VP4 had 20.

The collections were enlarged by projection — taking genomes whose own mat_peptide records are exact substrings of their own polyprotein, aligning every other polyprotein to its nearest such reference, and carrying the cut coordinates across. Nothing is predicted. A segment is kept only if the polyprotein is at least 50% identical to its reference, the segment falls inside the feature's window, and it is at least 35% identical to the reference segment.
3D went from 40 sequences to 203, 2C from 61 to 142, VP1 from 77 to 138, VPg from 9 to 37. The module now carries 86 profiles, and every feature built at the documented defaults.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Windows at 0.8× to 1.2× the collection median, bit cutoffs at 0.45× the median length with a floor of 20.

blocks.html: Self-recall against each feature's own in-range collection: 1023 of 1025 (99.8%) — POLY 337/338, VP4 25/25, VP2 41/41, VP3 52/52, VP1 110/110, 2A 47/47, 2B 12/13, 2C 115/115, 3A 51/51, VPG 9/9, 3C 54/54, 3D 170/170. This is a floor, not a validation; the held-out figures are in §05 and §06.

rows: genomes ≥ 5 kb, clustered at 95% nucleotide identity

blocks.html: 25 rep contigs ship with the module; 25 of them are the best BLASTn hit for at least one exemplar. Routing was measured against the ten Picornaviridae modules only — nucleotide BLASTn cannot reach the routing threshold across virus families, and leaving the other 56 modules' 558 rep contigs out cut the run time four-fold.

All three unrouted genomes are bird-associated: two Hepatovirus sp. from goose faeces and one mute swan hepatovirus. A genome no rep contig claims is never annotated at all, so these are a routing gap rather than a profile gap.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Eleven features on at least 99 of 113 exemplars, and 89 genomes carry all twelve.

blocks.html: 87 of 113 routed exemplars get every one of the 12 core features. No core feature trails the best-called one by 20 points or more. 1 routed exemplar(s) cleared no profile at any feature and are counted here as calling nothing.

VP4 is the lowest at 96 of 113. It is the shortest capsid protein in the genome, about 23 residues in this genus, and short proteins are where divergence costs most because there is less sequence over which a profile can accumulate score. The misses are concentrated in the non-primate species: 6 of 12 Hepatovirus sp., both bar-headed goose hepatoviruses, Loch Leven virus, and both mute swan hepatoviruses — against 2 of 59 for hepatitis A virus itself.
One routed exemplar clears no profile at any feature.

The panel is 39 genomes drawn round-robin across species from this genus's own BV-BRC contigs, with every rep-contig reference genome excluded, built into GTOs with rast-create-genome and scored by viral_genome_quality.pl. Genuinely clean means no genome, contig or feature flag at all.

sections.title: What it cannot do
sections.lede: The non-primate hepatoviruses, at both ends of the pipeline.

blocks.html: Hepatitis A virus itself is called completely — VP4 on 57 of 59 exemplars and every other feature at or near 100%. The module does the job it is principally needed for.

The bird hepatoviruses fail twice. Three of them do not route at all, so they are never annotated; of those that do route, both bar-headed goose genomes and both mute swan genomes miss VP4. These are the most recently described members of the genus and the most thinly sequenced, and the module has essentially nothing to learn them from.

Projection could not reach them either. It requires a reference polyprotein at least 50% identical, and the non-primate hepatoviruses are further from hepatitis A virus than that. So the rebuild that doubled this module improved it mostly where it was already adequate, and left the thin end thin. That is the honest shape of the result: more training data for the species that already had some.

VPg and 2B were refused by the cleavage-site test on 6 October and are no longer projected. For VPg, P1 is E in 79% of the references that place it — but the remaining 21% are four different residues (D, T, G and C), so the cut cannot be placed with confidence on a target that resembles them. For 2B, P1 is Q in 58%. Both keep their pre-projection collections (9 and 13 sequences) and both still build two profiles.

That cost the module 13 calls of 1,316, and the trade was deliberate. 2B fell 102→97, 3A 108→102, 2A 106→105 and VPg 99→98. Against that, 480 of this module's 1,602 projected sequences — 30% — had been carried across below 80% identity and are gone. A 1% loss in calls in exchange for removing a third of the training data that could not be trusted residue-by-residue is the right direction for an annotation module.

Gruhelivirus and Crahelivirus route here without being declared. Three of three and one of one exemplars respectively, at 8.3 and 9.0 features per genome, measured 6 October across the 404 genomes of the 36 genera no module claims.

Hepatitis A virus is covered completely. The non-primate hepatoviruses are covered partially and the bird hepatoviruses barely at all, failing both at routing and at VP4. Closing that needs annotated genomes from those lineages, not a threshold change or another projection pass.

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: The run showed what a thin collection costs, and what enlarging it does and does not buy.

blocks.html: This module was built correctly on 2 October from the data available and had 42 profiles behind twelve features. Nothing in the build, the install check or the cross-feature QC can report that a feature has too few training sequences; the profiles recovered their own data perfectly, because there was so little of it.

Doubling the collections moved the complete-genome count from 84 to 89 and lifted 2B and VPg by a few exemplars each. That is a real but modest gain, and it is worth stating plainly rather than presenting the doubling as a transformation — compare Sapelovirus, where the same technique moved the leader from 6 calls to 170. The difference is that Sapelovirus had a feature that was broken, while Hepatovirus had features that were merely thin.

sections.title: What the vocabulary bought
sections.lede: A well-named genus by this family's standards.

blocks.html: Rarefaction over proteins: every annotated protein in the 81 genomes both sources annotate (173 source product records, 927 module calls) shuffled 100 times and drawn one at a time. Both curves start at zero. The source vocabulary reaches 43 distinct strings, the module's 13. At the depth both reach, 173 proteins, free text has used 43.0 strings against 12.2 — a 3.5-fold difference. The source reaches 95% of its final size after 162 proteins, the module after 290.

Hepatovirus collapses at 6.3×, above the family median. Submitters of hepatitis A virus sequences are relatively consistent, and most of the variety the vocabulary absorbs comes from the recently described animal hepatoviruses.
